idiom_name: duck-typed implementor object stored in a field
implementation_notes: There is no interface to declare: the implementor is any object with the primitive methods, and the abstraction is a class (or factory function) that stores it in a field - a private # field where encapsulation matters - set by the constructor. MDN's prototype-chain documentation makes the same point from the language side: the mechanism is behaviour delegation, classes are sugar over it, so the implementor side needs no shared base at all. What replaces the classic two-hierarchy structure is composition plus duck typing, optionally with TypeScript or JSDoc types on the field; an abstract base is justified only when you want shared forwarding code or instanceof-based dispatch.
pitfalls: Nothing checks the implementor shape: a renamed primitive fails as TypeError: not a function at call time (or silently does nothing), so validate at the boundary or type the field.
Detached methods: passing renderer.circle as a callback loses its receiver; bind it or keep the object and call through it.
Private # fields are per-class brand checks, so a structurally identical plain object cannot be passed where a class with private state is expected.
